text.note: The real pair produced 1 changed block; +-16 antialiasing noise 13 and a 0.5-pixel shift 14, both below the threshold's 28 blocks; a whole-pixel shift 221 and the control's 24-pixel move 1272 are well above it. The class separates the two directions on a dense page. The 300-point page carries less ink: its blank page produces 47 changed blocks (above the class's 39-block allowance on its 15625 blocks), its whole-pixel shift 3 and its 24-pixel move 46, so the class is coarse there and does not claim per-pixel sensitivity.

picture.note: The real pair produced 0 changed blocks, a 0.5-pixel shift 19 and a whole-pixel shift 38, so the class separates the two directions at 34 blocks on the full-size picture; the control's 24-pixel move produces 280. The second picture page places the picture smaller, so its whole-pixel shift produces only 7 and its 24-pixel move 110; the class is coarse there. The two renderers resample images differently: the signal catches a missing, blank or grossly displaced picture, not a small colour shift.

annotation.note: The annotation's rectangle is rounded to device pixels differently by the two renderers: the real pair already differs by 31 blocks, and a whole-pixel shift (53) is not separable from a sub-pixel one (45). The class cannot separate the two and says so; its threshold is 67 blocks, which catches a blank page (397) and the control's 24-pixel move (228), not a one-pixel shift.
